decisions.reason: Because it is an adjacent extension of our wafer-substrate business and likely inexpensive to keep available while customers in long qualification cycles reveal demand, we would keep it.
Because carrier wafers for handling smaller wafers fit our core capabilities and customer base closely and require little additional commitment to preserve the option value, we would keep it.
Because the copper interposer glass wafer is a declared strategic focus with upside in advanced packaging and uncertainty about payoff is still resolving, we would keep it.
Because the off-the-shelf wafer brand is very close to our established offer, spans several models, and supports scalable commercialization at low marginal risk, we would keep it.

Because glass-based circuit boards are more distant from our core substrate niche and would demand broader commercial and technical follow-through than our narrow product strategy justifies, we would drop it.
